title: Device verification of meadow-snapshot-pacing at 0289cbbf: Note10+ floor regression, loop back through interphase amendment 2
context: Round 2 was green at 0289cbbf and device verification passed on Windows (10.12), the Android emulator (10.13, onboarding pass, held clause failing for both builds) and the macOS VM (10.14). The owner then connected the Galaxy Note10+ (Adreno 640, Impeller OpenGL ES), the floor device. There the fix regresses against the unchanged build. Onboarding drops from 33 to 15-17 fps and never sharpens, Meadow opens take about 4.1 s to full quality against 2.3 s, and time changes run 48.5 against 53.5 fps. Trials in the scratch tree isolate the cause: the per-batch toByteData readback marker blocks the raster thread until the GPU drains on OpenGL ES. Removing it on frames restores parity. Keeping one readback in flight with one batch ahead for frame-free work (oneflight) shows the scene at 990 ms against 1091 ms unchanged, with full quality 2.43 s against 2.27 s, onboarding 30.5-30.9 against 31.8-31.9 fps, and time changes at parity. Evidence: ~/.mitosis/field-notes/meadow-snapshot-pacing/review/device/note10-floor.md.
options: Loop back: interphase:bug amendment 2 on docs/specs/meadow-snapshot-pacing.md with the device finding D1 as the only concern, MSP label meadow-snapshot-pacing-amend-2, built with amend-2.zsh on mitosis/meadow-snapshot-pacing, then review round 3
Ship 0289cbbf and list the Note10+ regression as a known risk
Patch the MSP branch by hand with the oneflight trial
option_reasons: The regression is confirmed on the floor device the app targets, the cause is isolated by trial, and the pipeline sends every confirmed blocker back to interphase; the amendment keeps the criteria, tests and review of the fix
Shipping halves onboarding frame rate and drops quality on low-end Android, which breaks the owner's goal that the Meadow looks and performs as before or better everywhere
Hand edits skip the spec, the gates and the independent review the pipeline requires
outcome: Loop back with amendment 2. The concern is D1 in review/device/note10-floor.md. The direction comes from the trials: no readback for batches on frames, recolour pieces on frames bounded by the snapshot room and half the frame's UI time, and frame-free work keeping a GPU completion signal with at most one readback in flight and one batch recorded ahead. The amendment adds a Note10+ floor device criterion beside 10.12 to 10.14. Then amend-2.zsh plan-only and build, merge into mitosis/meadow-snapshot-pacing, review round 3 with previous_head 0289cbbf, and re-verify every device.
